content: 1. Doxylamine and imipramine both enhance sedative effects. Exercise caution and monitor the patient closely when these drugs are co-administered. 2. Doxylamine increases the effects of incobotulinumtoxinA through pharmacodynamic synergy. Use caution and monitor closely. Drugs with anticholinergic properties may amplify the effects of botulinum toxin, potentially leading to excessive neuromuscular weakness and heightened systemic anticholinergic effects. 3. Isocarboxazid significantly increases the effects of doxylamine. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Isocarboxazid should not be combined with antihistamines due to the risk of additive central nervous system (CNS) depressant effects. Monoamine oxidase inhibitors (MAOIs) also prolong and intensify the anticholinergic effects of antihistamines. 4. Isoniazid reduces pyridoxine levels through an unspecified mechanism. If the isoniazid dose exceeds 10 mg/kg/day, supplement with 50–100 mg of pyridoxine daily. Monitor closely. 5. Kava enhances the effects of doxylamine via pharmacodynamic synergy, potentially increasing CNS depression. Use caution and monitor closely. 6. Ketamine and doxylamine both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Doxylamine and ketotifen (ophthalmic) both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Lasmiditan and doxylamine mutually enhance each other’s sedative effects. Use caution and monitor closely. The combination of lasmiditan with other CNS depressants, including alcohol, has not been evaluated in clinical studies. Lasmiditan may cause sedation and other cognitive or neuropsychiatric adverse effects. 9. Lemborexant and doxylamine both increase sedation. Avoid or use an alternative drug.
